sources.entry: Orkas - Local-first multi-agent desktop application where a Commander coordinates specialist agents for research, coding, data analysis, documents, and media.

summary.one_liner: Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first desktop app where a Commander agent turns goals into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents plus external CLI agents such as Claude Code and Codex.
summary.what_it_does: Orkas lets you give a goal to a Commander agent, which handles general work itself and delegates specialist work to named agents (for example DeepResearcher, PptMaker, VideoStudio, OfficeWorker, ProductDeveloper and several e-commerce agents). Projects hold goals, rules, memory and files so new conversations continue earlier work. Each project has a to-do list shared by people and agents, with an Auto-advance option, and scheduled automations can repeat tasks hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. It can also run external CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent) as local sessions under one plan. A local Library indexes your documents for search with citations, and it supports OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible model endpoints, including local ones.
use_cases: Generating slide decks, documents and spreadsheets
Coordinating coding agents like Claude Code and Codex
Searching and asking questions about local documents with citations
E-commerce listing, review and sales analysis
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
Then open Settings → AI Providers to add an API key or OAuth
notable: Commander agent delegates via dispatch_to, hand_off_to and run_worker tools
Orchestrates external CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes-Agent) in one plan
Projects with memory, files, to-dos and Auto-advance that persist across conversations
Local-first: data, keys and Library index stay on disk; works with local model endpoints
Background reviews let agents refine their own self-assessment and learned skills
caveats: Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing exist only in the packaged app, not the open-source build
Automations and Auto-advance need the computer awake and Orkas running
Linux source builds need glibc 2.34+; Alpine/musl distributions are not supported; no Linux installer yet
